rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: **Not when stuck. Not after a round of tuning fails. BEFORE.** One search costs seconds; deriving by hand what a field settled decades ago costs a session
rules.says: Before starting each new piece of work, stop and look the thing up (not only when stuck or after tuning fails), because a search is cheap and deriving by hand what the field already settled costs a whole session.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: **This is a CADENCE, not a principle.** The difference matters: as a principle it gets agreed with and then skipped
rules.says: Looking things up is a cadence whose trigger is that a new piece of work is about to begin, and it fires every time whether or not the next step looks obvious enough not to need checking.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: **It was said three times in one repository before it was written here**, which is the standing signal that a rule belongs in the doctrine
rules.says: When the owner has said the same thing repeatedly (three times in a repository is the signal), it belongs in the doctrine, and the session that hears the repeat writes it down; that is not a decision to put to the owner.
rules.live_quote: Writing one is not a decision to put to the owner. A session that has just learned something and asks whether it should be recorded has turned a standing instruction into a request for permission
rules.missing: Only covers recording a lesson in LESSONS.md. Not stated live: that the owner saying the same thing repeatedly (three times in a repository is the signal) means the rule belongs in the doctrine, and that the session writes it into the doctrine.

rules.heading: 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: to mine the references for known things before implementing (2026-07-25)
rules.says: Before implementing, mine the references for what is already known.

rules.heading: 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: to go and learn the domain rather than converge inside the app (2026-09-16)
rules.says: Go and learn the domain from outside the app rather than converging on an answer by working only inside the app.

rules.heading: 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: bright foliage washing out to white — was about to be attacked by hand; one search named it as a known, standard consequence of applying a tone curve independently per channel
rules.says: Bright foliage washing out to white is a known, standard consequence of applying a tone curve independently per channel, with alternatives already named and parameterised elsewhere, so it is looked up and not derived by hand.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: **A measurement of your own output cannot tell you what the output should be.**
rules.says: Measuring the app's own output, however real the readings, cannot answer what the output should be, so a session must not treat self-measurement as a substitute for looking up the reference.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: **What counts as looking.** A search, a spec, a reference implementation, the file format's own documentation, the manual of the thing being emulated.
rules.says: Looking counts only as consulting an outside source: a search, a spec, a reference implementation, the file format's own documentation, or the manual of the thing being emulated.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: Write what is found into the repo's research file with the source named, so the next session does not pay for it again.
rules.says: What a lookup finds must be written into the repository's research file with the source named, so the next session does not pay for it again.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: A blocked host is a QUESTION asked in the moment, never a reason to fall back on what the model remembers (§0d).
rules.says: When a lookup is blocked by a blocked host, ask the owner in the moment and never fall back on what the model remembers.
rules.live_quote: ### 15c. A DENIED HOST IS A QUESTION FOR THE OWNER, NEVER A FINDING. ASK FOR IT BY NAME.
rules.missing: The ask-the-owner-for-a-denied-host part is stated. Not stated live: that a blocked lookup must never fall back on what the model remembers, and the tie to a look-it-up step.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: **So the cadence has a second trigger: every session start and every compaction, not the start of a task.** Before the first piece of work, and again after every compaction: run [`doctrine-sync.mjs`]
rules.says: The look-it-up cadence has a second trigger at every session start and every compaction (not at the start of a task): before the first piece of work and again after every compaction, run doctrine-sync.mjs, which the hub's CLAUDE.md says to run first.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: and read THIS WHOLE FILE — every line, not its section list and not a summary of it — so that adding to it is distinguishable from re-deriving it.
rules.says: At every session start and after every compaction, read the whole doctrine file line by line (not its section list or a summary), because a compaction summary of the doctrine is a paraphrase that drifts; how much is re-read after a compaction or resume is set in the paragraph that follows.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: **A session that writes a new rule without having read the existing ones is not learning, it is duplicating**
rules.says: A session must not write a new rule into the doctrine without having read the existing ones, because a duplicate makes the document longer and the next session less likely to read it.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: *Enforced by:* `doctrine-read-guard.mjs`, on the main thread. Every SessionStart, the one the harness fires after a compaction included, writes a due marker for the session
rules.says: Every SessionStart, including the one after a compaction, writes a due marker recording the start's source and printing one line saying what is due and naming the lines, and while the marker stands the main thread may only read and give the status.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: At a startup, a clear and a compaction every line is due: the read carries the owner's rules word for word across the point where a summary replaces the conversation
rules.says: At a startup, a clear and a compaction every line of the doctrine is due to be read, because a part of the file carries only a part of the owner's rules.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: After a resume nothing is due when the Read results in the session's transcript since its last startup or compaction cover every line of the doctrine as it stands; every line is due otherwise
rules.says: After a resume nothing is due only when the Read results in the transcript since the last startup or compaction cover every line of the doctrine as it now stands; otherwise every line is due, including when only a part was read, the whole was read only before the last compaction, or the file has since changed length.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: A doctrine whose lines cannot be counted is read in full.
rules.says: If the doctrine's lines cannot be counted, it must be read in full.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: The marker clears when the Read results on `doctrine/never.md` cover the lines due, counted across as many reads as it takes from the lines each result actually returned, never an errored one
rules.says: The due marker clears only when Read results on doctrine/never.md cover the lines due, counted across as many reads as it takes from lines each result actually returned and never an errored one: for a startup, clear or compaction those returned after the marker, for a resume those since the last compaction.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: Only the hub's own `doctrine/never.md` counts, the one beside the gate in the clone every gate runs from; a copy anywhere else is not the doctrine.
rules.says: Only the hub's own doctrine/never.md, the one beside the gate in the clone every gate runs from, counts as the doctrine for the read; a copy anywhere else does not.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: The plans page is due at the entry to plan mode, and the gate holds the main thread to reading until it has been read.
rules.says: The plans page must be read at the entry to plan mode, and the gate holds the main thread to reading only until it has been read.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: Agents are not held by it: `plan-fence.mjs` holds them to the approved plan instead (§11b).
rules.says: Agents (as opposed to the main thread) are not held by the doctrine-read gate; instead they are held to the approved plan.

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: *Enforced by:* `lessonCitedProblem` in `hook-dispatch.mjs`, called by `plan-guard.mjs` at `--check` and at the approval call (Q-HUB-306): a plan whose `## Steps` name a gate function in a code span
rules.says: A plan whose Steps name a gate function in a code span (letters and digits only, lower case first with a capital inside) must cite in its Design, as §N or as the word lesson and N, each lesson file whose text names that function, or it is refused naming the function and each missing number; it is a fault of the plan's shape and sets no latch.
rules.enforcer: lessonCitedProblem in hook-dispatch.mjs, called by plan-guard.mjs at --check and at the approval call (Q-HUB-306)

rules.heading: 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: It forces the account of earlier fixes and cannot judge that the account is true.
rules.says: The lesson-citation check only forces the plan to give an account of earlier fixes and cannot judge whether that account is true, so the session itself must make the account true.
rules.enforcer: lessonCitedProblem in hook-dispatch.mjs, called by plan-guard.mjs

rules.heading: ## 11e. STOP BEFORE EACH NEW THING AND GO AND LOOK IT UP
rules.quote: **The tell, stated so it can be caught early:** the urge to write a NEW rule is itself the signal to go and check whether it is already written.
rules.says: When a session feels the urge to write a new rule, treat that as the signal to first check whether it is already written, since a freshly discovered failure is most likely a rediscovery.

rules.heading: ## 11f. THREE ALTITUDES, AND THE RETURN TRIP IS THE ONE THAT GETS SKIPPED
rules.quote: Strategic — the whole app, and why it is shaped the way it is. Implementation — the actual call chain, the actual lines, traced. Then back up: **given the whole app, was this the right thing to have added?**
rules.says: Work at three altitudes: strategic (the whole app and why it is shaped that way), implementation (the actual call chain and lines, traced), then back up to ask whether, given the whole app, this was the right thing to have added.

rules.heading: ## 11f. THREE ALTITUDES, AND THE RETURN TRIP IS THE ONE THAT GETS SKIPPED
rules.quote: **The failure is living at a MIDDLE altitude**, which feels like both and is neither: too high to know what the code does, too low to see what the system is.
rules.says: Do not work at a middle altitude: reading two functions and calling it a diagnosis, or fitting a parameter until the output matches, produces confident prose that is grounded in nothing.

rules.heading: ## 11f. THREE ALTITUDES, AND THE RETURN TRIP IS THE ONE THAT GETS SKIPPED
rules.quote: **The return trip is a step with a question attached, not a summary.**
rules.says: The return trip is a step that asks whether the thing just built belongs in this app at all, it must be asked BEFORE the commit (afterwards it is only a defence), and a report of what was built does not count as it.

rules.heading: ## 11f. THREE ALTITUDES, AND THE RETURN TRIP IS THE ONE THAT GETS SKIPPED
rules.quote: **Neither altitude is home.** A session that only ever zooms out produces architecture essays it cannot cash
rules.says: A session must neither only zoom out nor only zoom in; the obligation is to traverse both ways, every time.

rules.heading: ## 11f. THREE ALTITUDES, AND THE RETURN TRIP IS THE ONE THAT GETS SKIPPED
rules.quote: **Enforced at the plan.** [`plan-guard.mjs`](plan-guard.mjs) refuses `ExitPlanMode` unless the plan's top block carries five sections with real bodies
rules.says: A plan's top block must carry five sections with real bodies (Looked up per §11e, Branches, Call chain, Whole app being the return trip, and Leaves open) or ExitPlanMode is refused.

rules.heading: ## 11f. THREE ALTITUDES, AND THE RETURN TRIP IS THE ONE THAT GETS SKIPPED
rules.quote: and *Leaves open* — each abandoned branch with WHERE it now lives, not a chat sentence.
rules.says: The Leaves open section must list each abandoned branch with where it now lives, not a chat sentence.

rules.heading: 11f. THREE ALTITUDES, AND THE RETURN TRIP IS THE ONE THAT GETS SKIPPED
rules.quote: The shape is the RFC template's, not invented here.
rules.says: The five-section plan shape follows the RFC template and is not an invention of the doctrine, so it is kept as that template defines it.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: - `NOTES.md` — the repo's source of truth: thesis, roadmap, settled decisions, Project facts. Read it first, every session.
rules.says: Each repo keeps NOTES.md as its source of truth (thesis, roadmap, settled decisions, project facts), and a session reads it first, every session.
rules.live_quote: 3. `NOTES.md` — the repo's source of truth (thesis, roadmap, settled decisions, Project facts).
rules.missing: The instruction that a session reads NOTES.md first, every session, is not stated live.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: - `CLAUDE.md` — repo-specific behavior + a pointer to THIS doctrine. Keep it thin.
rules.says: A repo's CLAUDE.md holds repo-specific behaviour plus a pointer to the hub doctrine and is kept thin.
rules.live_quote: Each repo's own `CLAUDE.md` should hold only repo-specific facts and a one-line pointer to this document — never re-state these rules (that is how they drift).

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: - `ACCESSIBILITY.md` — the append-only accessibility register, where used.
rules.says: Where used, ACCESSIBILITY.md is the append-only accessibility register.
rules.live_quote: 4. `ACCESSIBILITY.md` — if the app has any UI (the append-only register).

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: - `PALETTES.md` **in this hub** — [how any app gets reskinned](PALETTES.md): the colour ROLES (so one instrument serves apps that name their tokens differently), the hard floors
rules.says: Reskinning any app follows the hub's PALETTES.md, which defines the colour roles, the hard floors, the coupling that makes surfaces, text and rails a single system, four verified palette families and the measurement traps, and palette-check.mjs enforces it by exiting non-zero.
rules.live_quote: Before touching any palette, read [`PALETTES.md`](PALETTES.md) (roles, floors, four verified families, the measurement traps) and run [`palette-check.mjs`](palette-check.mjs).

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: Canonical HERE — link to it, never fork it.
rules.says: The hub's PALETTES.md is canonical: apps link to it and never fork a copy.
rules.live_quote: Canonical here in the hub, like DOCTRINE.md and LESSONS.md. **Never fork this into another repo — link to it.**
